Research Profile

Environmental scientist and geographer working on agricultural water quality, precision conservation, and spatial environmental decisions. I combine monitoring, geospatial analysis, machine learning, and process-based modelling to compare conservation options. My doctoral work provides the foundation for REAL Decision Lab, a developing research program linking environmental evidence with practical decisions. Earth observation and GeoAI (AI for geographic data) are emerging methods; food-system resilience is a developing direction.

Research Program and Current Projects
REAL Decision Lab - developing research program
Landscape Monitoring & Earth Observation: What is changing, where, and when?
Environmental Processes, Modelling & GeoAI: Why is it changing?
Precision & Multi-Benefit Conservation: What should be done, and where?
Adaptive Decision Support & Learning: What worked, and what should change next?
Observe -> Understand -> Plan -> Decide & Learn. Monitor outcomes, compare with expectations, learn, update models and priorities, and observe again.
Active: Healthy Lake Huron - Monitoring, Modelling and Conservation Decision Support. Connect watershed evidence with conservation scenarios and stewardship decisions.

Developing: Earth Observation & GeoAI for Agricultural Landscapes. Explore satellite and geographic data methods for monitoring agricultural landscapes.

Submitted proposal / developing: Food-System Resilience and Anticipatory Decision-Making. Investigate early stress signals and capacities that help food systems absorb stress. The CPRA proposal is submitted; no fellowship award is claimed.
